title: Audit and traceability
subtitle: Record enough to reconstruct what the assistant did, without the record becoming a new problem
mission: On a Thursday, a person claims the assistant said you could sell half of your vacation. To investigate, the team must reconstruct that answer: when it was, which prompt version and model were live, which documents entered the context. Aurora’s audit trail records one event per answer. Choose the fields, what to do with the conversation text and how to protect the file against editing, and see which incident questions the trail can answer.

why.simples:
An audit trail is the airplane’s black box: it does not prevent the accident, but it lets you find out what happened and fix it. For that it must keep enough (who, when, what was used) and be protected against editing, otherwise anyone "tidies up" the story afterwards.
And there is the other end: if the black box records everything every passenger said, including what was private, it becomes a danger itself. The rule is to record what explains the decision, not whatever is possible.
why.dev:
One event per answer, in JSON, with fixed fields: id, date and time, user code (pseudonym), prompt version, model id (such as claude-sonnet-5-5), ids and versions of the documents that entered the context, each guardrail’s decisions, tokens and cost, and the already redacted question and answer. With that you reconstruct an answer: same prompt, same documents, same model. Without the prompt and document versions, you cannot reproduce it; without the user, you cannot answer "who saw this"; without the guardrail decisions, you cannot prove the attack was blocked.
Integrity: chain the events with a hash (each line stores the previous line’s hash). Editing a line breaks the chain from there on. Whoever controls the file can still recompute everything, so publish the latest hash on a separate system from time to time, and write to append-only storage when the provider offers it.
Privacy: redacted text (previous lesson), role-based access with a record of who read the log, a retention period and pseudonym identification, to handle one person’s requests. If the log also feeds the evaluation set, redact before copying.
why.especialista:
Recording and accountability show up in the law and in management frameworks. In LGPD, art. 37 requires controller and operator to keep a record of personal data processing operations, art. 6, X asks for accountability (showing effective measures) and art. 48 requires notifying security incidents to the ANPD and the data subject; under Resolution CD/ANPD 15/2024, the deadline is three business days from knowing about the incident, and without a trail you cannot say in three days who was affected. Art. 20 gives data subjects the right to request review of decisions made solely on automated processing, which requires being able to explain how the decision was produced.
NIST AI RMF 1.0 (January 2023) organizes AI risk management in four functions, Govern, Map, Measure and Manage, and the generative AI profile NIST AI 600-1 (July 2024) applies it to 12 risks. ISO/IEC 42001:2023, published in December 2023, defines requirements for an AI management system in an organization. In any audit based on this kind of reference, records of what the system did are the natural evidence.
The balance is hard: the trail needs detail to prove something and restraint not to be a second repository of personal data. Decide, in writing, who may read the trail, for how long it stays and what is redacted, and review it with the data protection officer.

steps:
Create audit.py: records one event per answer with a chained hash and verifies the whole chain:
import hashlib
import json
import pathlib
import time
import uuid

LOG = pathlib.Path("audit.jsonl")


def _hash(prev, record):
    body = json.dumps(record, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False)
    return hashlib.sha256((prev + body).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()


def _last_hash():
    if not LOG.exists():
        return "0" * 64
    lines = LOG.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
    return json.loads(lines[-1])["hash"] if lines else "0" * 64


def write_event(user_code, prompt_v, model, docs, guards, tokens, question, answer):
    """Um evento por resposta. question e answer chegam JÁ redigidos (veja a lição de LGPD)."""
    record = {
        "id": str(uuid.uuid4()),
        "ts": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", time.gmtime()),
        "user": user_code,            # pseudônimo, nunca o nome
        "prompt_v": prompt_v,         # ex.: "rh-v3"
        "model": model,               # ex.: "claude-sonnet-5-5"
        "docs": docs,                 # ids (e versões) dos documentos que entraram no contexto
        "guards": guards,             # ex.: {"input": "allow", "output": "allow"}
        "tokens": tokens,             # {"in": 812, "out": 96}
        "question": question,
        "answer": answer,
        "prev": _last_hash(),
    }
    record["hash"] = _hash(record["prev"], {k: v for k, v in record.items() if k != "hash"})
    with LOG.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(json.dumps(record, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
    return record["id"]


def verify():
    """Devolve None se a cadeia está íntegra, ou o número da primeira linha adulterada."""
    prev = "0" * 64
    for n, line in enumerate(LOG.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines(), start=1):
        record = json.loads(line)
        body = {k: v for k, v in record.items() if k != "hash"}
        if record["prev"] != prev or record["hash"] != _hash(prev, body):
            return n
        prev = record["hash"]
    return None

Add a tampering test to the end of the file and run it:
if __name__ == "__main__":
    pathlib.Path("audit.jsonl").unlink(missing_ok=True)
    for i in range(3):
        write_event("u-9f3a", "rh-v3", "claude-sonnet-5-5", ["manual-ferias@2026-10"], {"input": "allow", "output": "allow"},
                    {"in": 800 + i, "out": 90}, "Why did the assistant say you can sell half of your vacation?", "Up to one third of your vacation.")
    print("cadeia íntegra?", verify() is None)
    lines = LOG.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
    lines[1] = lines[1].replace("one third", "half")        # alguém "arruma" a evidência
    LOG.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    print("primeira linha adulterada:", verify())
python audit.py

Call write_event() at the same point in the code where the answer is returned, with the text already redacted. Schedule a daily check (verify()) and send the latest hash to a separate system. Define in writing who reads the trail and how long it stays.
recipe.ok: the test prints "cadeia íntegra? True" and then "primeira linha adulterada: 2": editing one word in the second line breaks its hash and the chaining of the following ones.
